messages.message:
Patch Set 1:

(3 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Mostly good, comments inline. The Makefile.am side checks out - rootsbin is a user-defined prefix with no "exec" in it, so automake really does install mount.lustre from install-data-am, and install-rootsbinPROGRAMS already runs $(MKDIR_P) on $(DESTDIR)$(rootsbindir) before the hook fires, so dropping the mkinstalldirs is fine.

One broader thought: this bug survived a whole release because nothing ever checked which filesystem type a target actually got mounted with. Would it be worth having mount_facet() confirm /proc/mounts shows lustre_tgt after a $MOUNT_TGT mount, so a silent fallback to '-t lustre' fails loudly next time instead of quietly passing?

commit.message:
LU-12514 utils: Build a real mount.lustre_tgt in a build tree

mount.lustre reads the fstype from argv[0], but in a build tree it
is a libtool wrapper that execs the hard-coded .libs/lt-mount.lustre,
so a mount.lustre_tgt symlink to it quietly mounts with '-t lustre'.
Build a real mount.lustre_tgt so it can be tested from the build
tree, and keep installing it as a symlink.

Move that symlink to install-data-hook, which runs after mount.lustre
is installed.

Fixes: 58adf0b4aaf1 ("LU-12514 tests: add testing for lustre_tgt type")
Signed-off-by: Xiao Yang <xyang@ddn.com>
Change-Id: I1ffdfafa0a127ba12b371e61d14a2ce49389f9bf
